paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: Accuracy of Llama4 Scout (top) and Llama4 Maverick (bottom) on 5-digit multiplication.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for an LLM (presumably Llama4 Scout, as indicated by the caption) on 5-digit multiplication tasks. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans a linear range from 0.95 to 0.99, with tick marks at 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98, and 0.99. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges linearly from 0.0 to 1.0, with major ticks every 0.2 units. The blue solid line with circle markers represents “Final Acc,” which remains relatively stable around 0.88–0.90 across the confidence range, peaking slightly near 0.98 before declining to ~0.87 at 0.99. The orange dashed line with diamond markers, labeled “Δ Acc,” starts at ~0.89 at 0.95, dips slightly to ~0.85 at 0.96, rises to ~0.87 at 0.97, then declines steadily to ~0.76 at 0.99. The green dotted line with square markers, labeled “Initial Acc,” remains near zero across all confidence levels, rising only slightly to ~0.12 at 0.99. Error bars are present for all data points, indicating variability in measurements.
